caption: LUM-1360 chatinput A/B: the composer's word-motion and readline vocabulary, driven in a real 80x26 PTY against the real binary. Panel 5 (`Alt+F`) is the A/B pair for the LUM-1360 defect: before the fix the global `app.session.fork` binding consumed `alt+f` and the frame showed `/fork: no session database`; after it, `alt+f` is `tui.editor.cursorWordRight` and the caret hops right, matching codex `move_word_right`, Martty `WordRight` and upstream `cursorWordRight`. Composer row is y=23, prompt prefix is x=0..1.

panels.label: 2. three words typed; caret at the end of the draft

probe.why: a plain draft renders with the block caret at the end

panels.label: 3. Ctrl+W deletes one word backward (codex, Martty and pi-ts all bind this)

probe.why: `gamma` is gone and the caret sits where it was

panels.label: 4. Alt+B hops one word left (esc-b; untouched by the LUM-1360 defect)

probe.why: the caret stops at the start of `beta`; the frame trims the draft's trailing space

panels.label: 5. Alt+F hops one word right — the LUM-1360 fix (before: this forked the session)

probe.why: the caret is back at the end of `beta`, one word right; the frame trims the draft's trailing space

reject.why: the fork picker must NOT run: `alt+f` is the editor's forward-word chord, not `app.session.fork` (LUM-1360). This row is a hard FAIL, so the pre-fix binary fails this scenario.

panels.label: 6. Ctrl+A / Ctrl+E are line-scoped, not draft-scoped

probe.why: Ctrl+A put the caret at the start of the only line

panels.label: 7. Ctrl+K kills to the end of the line and Ctrl+Y yanks it back

probe.why: the kill ring round-trips the whole killed tail

panels.label: 8. Ctrl+J opens a second draft row instead of submitting

probe.why: line 1 keeps its content (Ctrl+J did not submit)
line 2 is a real draft row with the caret at its end

panels.label: 9. double-click inside the composer selects the word under the pointer

probe.why: the draft is intact after the double click

panels.label: 10. a drag that starts in the composer extends the selection as the pointer moves left

probe.why: the draft survives a drag that leaves the composer body

panels.label: 11. Ctrl+C clears the draft on the first press (no exit)

probe.why: the composer is back to its placeholder and the process is alive

panels.label: 12. Enter submits, the transcript echoes the prompt

probe.why: the submitted prompt is echoed in the transcript

panels.label: 13. Up on the empty composer recalls it from the prompt history

probe.why: history recall puts the prompt back in the composer

panels.label: 14. Ctrl+R opens the reverse search over the prompt history

probe.why: the reverse search lists the matching history entry
